requirements.statement: Implement Phase 0 — Provenance decision and inventory from TAILTRAIL-BUNDLED-OFFLINE-AIDLC-PROVISIONING-DESIGN.md by extending scripts/aidlc-official-install.py to verify and record aidlc-rules/PROVENANCE.json, aidlc-rules/LICENSE, and aidlc-rules/VERSION against one pinned official AIDLC tag, full commit, archive SHA-256, complete rule inventory, bundle and official version semantics, TailTrail compatibility range, authenticated release trust anchor, four trust postures, source-checkout development-local contract, and approved v1/v2, active-run, external-pack, and host-projection decisions; exclude packaging manifests, resolver behavior, Full routing, and host adapters.

path_bindings.ownership_evidence: The Phase 0 design assigns this checked-in acquisition and verification receipt to the existing official installer owner.
The Phase 0 design requires the verified upstream MIT-0 license to be emitted beside the bundle by the existing official installer owner.

proof_bindings.asserted_behavior: The existing acquisition owner emits and validates complete Phase 0 provenance, license, version, compatibility, inventory, and trust metadata.
The checked-in Phase 0 outputs remain bound to one verified official source identity and do not grant authority to later packaging, routing, or host phases.

positive: The existing official acquisition and verification owner produces a checked-in Phase 0 provenance receipt and MIT-0 license bound to one pinned official tag, full commit, and archive SHA-256.
Every retained bundled rule byte is inventoried and matched to the pinned upstream source before official provenance is claimed.

Bundle version, official version, TailTrail compatibility, four trust postures, source-checkout posture, schema migration, active-run, external-pack, and host-projection decisions are explicit and internally consistent.
The provenance receipt, license, version fields, inventory, and retained acquisition evidence agree on one source identity.
negative: The existing aidlc-rules/VERSION value alone must not be treated as provenance.
Unverified current rule bytes must not be labelled as an official release.
Phase 0 must not change packaging manifests, resolver behavior, Full-mode routing, host adapters, or project projection state.
No runtime network dependency, silent Full-to-Lite fallback, weakened integrity rule, or fabricated provenance evidence may be introduced.
